naca0012_ladson.source: Ladson CL. Effects of independent variation of Mach and Reynolds numbers on the low-speed aerodynamic characteristics of the NACA 0012 airfoil section. NASA TM-4074, 1988 (NTRS 19880019495); tripped data at M 0.15, Re 6e6 as used by the NASA Turbulence Modeling Resource 2D NACA 0012 validation case
naca0012_ladson.grade: A for cl(10 deg) and cd0 (several validation reports quote the same runs); B for cl(15 deg)

naca0012_mccroskey.source: McCroskey WJ. A critical assessment of wind tunnel results for the NACA 0012 airfoil. NASA TM-100019 / AGARD CP-429, 1987 (NTRS 19880002254)

naca2412_thin_airfoil.source: Thin-airfoil theory integral of the NACA 2412 mean line (Abbott & von Doenhoff, Theory of Wing Sections, §4.3; worked in Anderson, Fundamentals of Aerodynamics, example 4.x); experimental alpha_L0 about -2 deg (Abbott & von Doenhoff appendix data via VT Aerodynamics and Aircraft Performance, app. A)

joukowski.source: Exact potential flow about a Joukowski airfoil by conformal mapping z = zeta + b^2/zeta of a circle of radius R centred at (-mx, my) through zeta = b: Gamma = 4 pi V R sin(alpha + beta), beta = asin(my/R) (Kutta-Joukowski; Katz & Plotkin, Low-Speed Aerodynamics, 2nd ed. §6.6; Milne-Thomson, Theoretical Aerodynamics). cl = 8 pi R sin(alpha+beta)/c with c the mapped chord.

acceptance.note: uniform panels in the circle angle; the cusped trailing edge converges at first order (1.3 % at 150/side, 0.46 % at 300/side, 0.21 % at 600/side for case 2)

lifting_line.source: Prandtl lifting-line theory: elliptic loading gives CL_alpha = a0/(1 + a0/(pi AR)) and CDi = CL^2/(pi AR), e = 1 exactly (Glauert 1926; Anderson §5.3.1). Helmbold 1942 low-AR correction for comparison.

skin_friction.source: Blasius 1908 laminar flat plate Cf = 1.328/sqrt(Re); Prandtl-Schlichting 1932 Cf = 0.455/(log10 Re)^2.58; 1/7 power law 0.074/Re^0.2; ITTC-1957 0.075/(log10 Re - 2)^2 (Schlichting, Boundary-Layer Theory; ITTC 1957 proceedings; cross-checked in AeroSandbox 4.2.10 viscous.py)

bluff_bodies.source: NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics, 'Shape Effects on Drag' (flat plate normal to the flow Cd 1.28); sphere about 0.47 at Re 1e4-2e5 (F. M. White, Fluid Mechanics, table 7.3)
